html:
Alwa, also called Alodia, was a Christian kingdom on the middle Nile in what is now Sudan, with its capital at Soba, near modern Khartoum. It lasted from about the 6th century to about 1500.

It was the southernmost of three kingdoms that rose in Nubia after the fall of Kush. To the north lay Nobatia and Makuria; Alwa held the rich land where the Blue and White Niles meet, and the plains between them. The kings of Aksum to the east already knew the area and raided it.

Missionaries from the Byzantine world converted the court around 580. For centuries afterward Alwa was a Christian kingdom with Greek and Coptic in its church, like its Nubian neighbours.

  • When the Arab armies took Egypt in the 640s, Makuria held them off and signed the Baqt treaty, a long peace. Alwa, further south, was sheltered behind it.
  • Arab writers of the 10th century described Soba as a large, wealthy town with many churches, gardens and markets.
  • Alwa traded across the region, with links reaching toward the Ethiopian highlands.

From the 12th or 13th century the kingdom seems to have weakened and broken up. Arab nomads moved south into its lands, and Islam spread. It fell around 1500, and the Funj Sultanate took over the region. By the early 1500s Soba was in ruins. Much of Alwa's history is still unknown, since few written sources survive and few sites have been dug.
sum: Alwa, also called Alodia, was a Christian kingdom on the middle Nile in what is now Sudan, with its capital at Soba, near modern Khartoum. It lasted from about the 6th century to about 1500.
